definition_zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子；拼合
definition_en: a part cut or broken from something larger; a single work of art or music; one of the objects moved in a board game; to join parts into a whole
core_image: 一块带釉的碎瓷片躺在桌上，断口处仍泛着光
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱落地，一只旧碗碎成几块，最大的那块还带着半圈蓝花。She picked up the largest piece and turned it over in her hand.
sceneCN: 这里 piece 指「一块、一片」（第 1 个义项：从整体上分下来的一部分）；句意为她捡起最大的那一块，在手里翻看。图中可辨识物件：碎瓷片、蓝花、落地的纸箱。

pos.zh: 一块；一片；一件；作品；棋子

derivatives.zh: 由 piece 加古英语后缀 -meal（逐……地）构成，义为「一件一件的；零碎的」
由 a 与 piece 合成，义为「每人；各」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，义为「杰作」

senses.title: A part broken or cut from something larger
senses.definition: a part separated from a whole, especially one small enough to hold or to see as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 从整体上分离出来的一部分，尤指小到可以拿在手里或单独看见的一块
senses.example: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。
senses.why: Medieval Latin petia named a fragment, and English took the word with that broken-off shape already inside it, so the first sense is the shard rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 本指碎片，英语借来时，「从整体上断下来的一块」这个形状已经装在词里，所以最早的义项是碎片而非整体。

senses.title: A single work of art, music, or writing
senses.definition: one complete work, especially a short musical composition, a painting, or a short text
senses.definitionCN: 一件完整的作品，尤指短小的乐曲、一幅画或一段短文
senses.example: The band played a new piece at the end of the set.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在演出末尾演奏了一首新作品。
senses.why: A work is also a unit that can be counted and handed over, so the noun that counted fragments came to count finished works, each treated as one whole.
senses.whyCN: 作品同样是可以清点、可以交到别人手里的一个单位，于是原本数碎块的名词也用来数成品，每一件都被当作一个整体。

senses.title: One of the objects moved in a board game
senses.definition: one of the small objects that a player moves on a board, as in chess or draughts
senses.definitionCN: 棋手在棋盘上移动的小物件之一，如国际象棋或跳棋中的棋子
senses.example: He moved a single piece and the whole game turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。
senses.why: A game set is a collection of small separate units, and each one is literally a piece taken out of the box, which is why the word needed no stretching here.
senses.whyCN: 一副棋就是一小堆彼此分开的小单位，每一枚本来就是从盒子里取出来的一块，所以这个词在这里根本不必引申。

senses.title: To join parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put the separate parts of something together until they form a whole, often by patient work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分开的各个部分合在一起，直到形成整体，常需耐心
senses.example: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: what was broken into pieces is put back, and the word now watches the fragments travel toward a whole instead of away from it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向倒过来：被分成块的东西重新合起来，这个词现在看着碎块朝整体走，而不是从整体散开。

intro.en: Piece came through Old French from a medieval Latin word for a fragment, and that word's own earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: piece 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语中表示碎片的一个词，而那个词更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin petia or petium meant a piece or fragment, but its earlier origin is uncertain and a Gaulish source is often suggested.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium 意为一块、碎片，但它更早的来源不确定，常有人推测来自高卢语。

items.en: Old French piece named a part, a fragment, or a coin, and carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 piece 指一部分、碎片或一枚钱币，诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English piece could mean a fragment, a share, or a particular item, and the spelling settled without the French accent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 piece 可指碎片、份额或某一件事物，拼写逐渐定型，去掉了法语的变音记号。

items.en: By the sixteenth century a piece could be a work of art or music, because such a work is exactly one countable item.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，piece 已可指一件艺术品或一首乐曲，因为这样一件作品恰好就是一个可以清点的事项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fragment at the centre and builds phrasal verbs such as piece together, where the fragments are put back.
items.cn: 现代英语仍以碎片为中心，并造出 piece together 这类短语动词，让碎片重新拼回去。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from a fragment, and its family keeps counting parts, works, and small movable units.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从碎片出发，它的词族一直在数部分、作品和可以移动的小单位。

normal.en: Piece came from Old French, and the medieval Latin form behind it already meant a fragment.
normal.cn: piece 来自古法语，而它背后的中世纪拉丁语形式本就已经指碎片。

normal.en: Piece together is the noun turned into a verb: the fragments are made to travel back into a whole.
normal.cn: piece together 是名词转成动词：碎块被赶回整体里去。

normal.en: Peace sounds exactly the same but comes from a different root, so the two must be kept apart in writing.
normal.cn: peace 读音完全相同，但来自另一个词根，所以写的时候必须把两者分开。

normal.en: Apiece adds a to piece and means one for each, as in tickets at ten pounds apiece.
normal.cn: apiece 在 piece 前加 a，意为「每人一个」，如门票每张十英镑。

normal.en: A piece of music and a piece of news both use piece as a counter for one item, not as a fragment.
normal.cn: 「一首乐曲」与「一则消息」里的 piece 都是清点事项的量词用法，而不是碎片。

abstract.en: The same word counts a broken shard, a finished sonata and a chessman, because English counts parts and wholes with one noun.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既数碎瓷片，也数写完的奏鸣曲和一枚棋子，因为英语用一个名词同时数部分与整体。

abstract.en: To piece something together is to trust that the fragments still carry the shape of what they came from.

senses.title: A person who flies an aircraft
senses.definition: a person trained and licensed to fly an aeroplane or other aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练并取得执照、驾驶飞机的人
senses.example: The pilot warned the passengers about the turbulence ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员提醒乘客前方有气流颠簸。
senses.why: The word first named the person who steers a ship; when machines took to the air, the same steering role handed the title to the flyer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指掌舵行船的人；当机器飞上天空，同一个「掌舵」的角色把称号交给了驾驶飞机的人。

senses.title: A specialist who guides a ship in harbour
senses.definition: a local expert who comes aboard to steer a ship through a harbour or a difficult channel
senses.definitionCN: 登船引导船只通过港口或复杂航道的当地专家
senses.example: A local pilot came aboard to take the ship through the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 一名当地引水员登船，带这艘船穿过狭窄航道。
senses.why: In a harbour the captain hands over control to someone who knows every sandbank, so the oldest sense of a hired guide at the helm survives intact.
senses.whyCN: 在港口，船长会把控制权交给熟悉每一处沙洲的人，于是「受雇掌舵的向导」这个最古老的义项完整地留了下来。

senses.title: To steer or guide something
senses.definition: to steer an aircraft, boat or vehicle, or to guide a process through its early stages
senses.definitionCN: 操纵飞机、船只或车辆，或引导某个过程走过最初阶段
senses.example: She piloted the boat through the gap in the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 她驾着小船穿过礁石间的缺口。
senses.why: English turns a role into a verb very readily, so whoever is the pilot simply does the piloting.
senses.whyCN: 英语很习惯把角色直接变成动词，所以当 pilot 的人做的事就叫 pilot。

senses.title: Done as a trial before a full launch
senses.definition: made or done on a small scale first, in order to test whether a full version will work
senses.definitionCN: 先小规模做出或进行，用来检验完整版本是否可行
senses.example: The company ran a pilot scheme in three cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在三座城市试行了一个方案。
senses.why: A pilot boat goes out ahead of the fleet to test the water, so the first small version of a project borrowed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 引水船会先于船队出海探路，于是项目最初的小规模版本也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Pilot came into English from the sea, through French and Italian, and its medieval Latin form is the first clearly recorded one; the step before that is disputed.
intro.cn: pilot 从海上经法语和意大利语进入英语，中世纪拉丁语形式是最早清楚可考的形态；再往前的一步则有争议。

items.en: One old suggestion traces the word to Greek pedon, an oar; the link is attractive but has never been proved, so it is best marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 一种旧说法把这个词追到希腊语 pedon（桨）；这条线索很吸引人，但从未得到证实，最好标为不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin pilotus named the man who steers a ship, and it is the earliest form that can be quoted with confidence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 pilotus 指掌舵行船的人，是能够有把握引用的最早形态。

items.en: Italian pilota carried the nautical sense across Mediterranean trade routes.
items.cn: 意大利语 pilota 沿地中海贸易路线传播了这个航海义。

items.en: Middle French pilot brought the word into English in the fifteenth century, still tied to ships and harbours.
items.cn: 中古法语 pilot 在十五世纪把这个词带进英语，当时仍与船和港口绑定。

items.en: Modern English moved the word from harbour to airfield, then to any small trial that goes first.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从港口搬到了机场，再延伸到任何先走一步的小规模试验。

definition_zh: 怜悯；同情；遗憾；可惜；同情（某人）
definition_en: a feeling of sorrow for the suffering of others, a cause for mild regret, or to feel sorry for someone
core_image: 雨中的长椅上，一个人把伞倾向旁边瑟缩的陌生人，自己的肩膀却湿了
scene: 冬天的车站外，一位老人蹲在湿冷的地上整理散落的行李，路过的年轻人停下脚步，弯下腰帮他捡。She felt a sudden pity for the old man in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「怜悯、同情」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难的难过与关切）；句意为她忽然对雨中的老人心生怜悯。画面里是弯腰帮忙捡行李的年轻人。

derivatives.zh: 由 pity 加 -ful 构成，义为「可怜的；令人同情的」，也可指「少得可怜的」
由 pity 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无情的；冷酷的」
由 self 与 pity 复合而成，指「自怜」

senses.title: Sympathy for another person's suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of sorrow and concern for someone who is suffering or unlucky
senses.definitionCN: 对正在受苦或遭遇不幸的人产生的难过与关切
senses.example: He looked at the injured bird with pity.
senses.exampleCN: 他怜悯地看着那只受伤的鸟。
senses.why: Latin pietas began as dutiful loyalty toward the gods and one's family, and Christian writers bent it toward tender concern for the weak, which is the feeling English now calls pity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pietas 起初指对神明与家人尽责的忠诚，基督教文献把它弯向对弱者的温柔关切；英语接过的正是这份「心里为别人发软」的感觉，所以怜悯义带着「本该关怀」的底色。

senses.title: A cause for mild regret
senses.definition: something that is a shame or a cause for mild regret
senses.definitionCN: 令人觉得惋惜、可惜的事
senses.example: It is a pity that the concert was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会取消了，真可惜。
senses.why: When sympathy is aimed at a situation rather than a person, it cools into mild regret, and the fixed phrase a pity carries that lighter, almost polite disappointment.
senses.whyCN: 当同情不是对着某个人，而是对着一件事，它就降温成轻微的惋惜；固定说法 a pity 承载的正是这种较轻、几乎带点客气的失望。

senses.title: To feel sorry for someone
senses.definition: to feel sorrow or sympathy for someone because of their suffering
senses.definitionCN: 因某人受苦而为他感到难过、同情
senses.example: I pity anyone who has to work outside in this weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这种天气还得在户外干活的人，我替他们难过。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling into a verb without changing its form, so the noun of compassion became a verb naming the act of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一种情感直接拿来当动词，词形不变；表示同情心的名词于是变成动词，指「生出这份同情」的动作。

intro.en: Pity comes from Latin pietas, dutiful loyalty, through French, and the religious duty softened into compassion before English took the word over.
intro.cn: pity 经法语来自拉丁语 pietas（尽责的忠诚）；那份宗教性的本分在进入英语之前，已经软化成同情。

items.en: Pius meant dutiful, loyal and reverent, first toward the gods and then toward family and country.
items.cn: pius 意为尽责的、忠诚的、虔敬的，最初对神明而言，后来也用于家人与国家。

items.en: Pietas named that dutiful loyalty; early Christian writers used it for compassionate devotion, and the emotional colour grew stronger.
items.cn: pietas 指这种尽责的忠诚；早期基督教作者用它来表示带着慈悲的虔敬，情感色彩因此变浓。

items.en: Old French pite took the word from Latin and made compassion its main sense.
items.cn: 古法语 pite 从拉丁语接过这个词，并把「怜悯」定为主要词义。

items.en: Middle English pite or pity meant tender sympathy and, in the phrase it is pity, also a matter for regret.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pite 或 pity 既指温柔的同情，也在 it is pity 这样的说法里指令人惋惜的事。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun and the verb, and the everyday phrase a pity now often means simply what a shame.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了名词与动词两种用法，日常说法 a pity 如今常常就等于「真可惜」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for sympathy and for mild regret.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示同情与轻微惋惜的词。

entries.definitionCN: 毫不同情的；冷酷无情的。

entries.definition: A very small amount of money or food; it also descends from Latin pietas.

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for duty, a Christian shade of compassion and a French narrowing all lead to the double English life of sympathy and mild regret.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示本分的拉丁词、一层基督教的慈悲色彩，再加上法语中的收窄，最终汇成英语里「同情」与「轻微惋惜」的双重用法。

normal.en: Latin pius meant dutiful, and pietas meant that duty; pity keeps the warmth of duty but loses the religious edge.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pius 意为尽责的，pietas 意为这份本分；pity 保留了本分里的温度，却丢掉了宗教的锋利边缘。

normal.en: French pite narrowed the word to compassion before English borrowed it, so the emotional sense arrived first.
normal.cn: 法语 pite 在英语借入之前已把词义收窄到「怜悯」，所以情感义是最先到达的。

normal.en: The phrase a pity turns sympathy toward a fact rather than a person, which is why it means a shame rather than mercy.
normal.cn: a pity 把同情从人转向一件事，所以它的意思是「可惜」，而不是「宽恕」。

normal.en: Pitiful and pitiless split the same stem in opposite directions: one invites pity, the other refuses it.
normal.cn: pitiful 与 pitiless 把同一个词干拉向相反方向：一个招来怜悯，一个拒绝怜悯。

normal.en: The verb pity needs no ending of its own; it simply puts the noun form in front of an object.
normal.cn: 动词 pity 不必另加词尾，直接把名词形式放在宾语前面就行。

abstract.en: Pity is duty that has forgotten its rules and kept only its tenderness.
abstract.cn: 怜悯是忘了规矩、只留下温柔的那份本分。

abstract.en: The same word can look down at a wounded bird and shrug at a cancelled concert, because sorrow cools into regret when nobody is suffering.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能低头看一只受伤的鸟，也能对一场取消的音乐会耸耸肩，因为当没有人正在受苦时，难过就降温成了惋惜。

abstract.en: Saying I pity you can comfort or condescend, which shows how close sympathy stands to distance.
abstract.cn: 说一句 I pity you，既可能是在安慰，也可能带着居高临下，可见同情与距离挨得有多近。

examples.en: He looked at the injured bird with pity.
examples.cn: 他怜悯地看着那只受伤的鸟。

examples.en: It is a pity that the concert was cancelled.
examples.cn: 音乐会取消了，真可惜。

examples.en: I pity anyone who has to work outside in this weather.
examples.cn: 这种天气还得在户外干活的人，我替他们难过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「批踢」——看到挨批又被踢的人，忍不住生出同情；pity 就是怜悯与遗憾。

root: 拉丁语 pius（尽责的、虔敬的）构成 pietas（虔敬、忠诚），经古法语 pite 进入英语；同族词多与虔敬、同情以及「少得可怜的一点东西」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hand reaching toward someone who is suffering; from that warmth come the noun of compassion, the verb of feeling it and the cooler regret of a pity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一只手伸向正在受苦的人；同情心的名词、生出同情的动词，以及较冷的「a pity」之叹，都从这份温度里分出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by bending down in the rain to help a stranger gather a spilled bag.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中的路人弯下腰，帮陌生人捡起散落一地的行李。

branches.cn: 双手小心捧着一只鸟

branches.en: a coat offered without being asked

intro.en: A Latin adjective of duty, its noun, a French form and two English suffixes that pull the word toward pity and away from it hold it together.
intro.cn: 一个表示本分的拉丁形容词、它的名词、一个法语形式，以及两个把词义拉向同情和拉离同情的英语后缀，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is secure: pius supplies the adjective of duty and pietas the noun that French and English softened into compassion.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的拉丁来历是可靠的：pius 提供表示本分的形容词，pietas 提供名词，二者经法语与英语软化成「怜悯」。

definition_zh: 地方；地点；座位；名次；放置
definition_en: a particular position or area; a seat kept for one person; a rank in a competition; and to put something in a particular position
core_image: 广场中央空出的一块干净石板地
scene: 集市散去的午后，广场上腾出一大片石板地。She stood in the middle of the empty market place and listened to the pigeons.
sceneCN: 这里 place 是「地方、地点」（第 1 个义项：某个具体的位置或区域）；句意为她站在空下来的集市空地上，听着鸽子叫。图中可辨识物件：石板地、空摊位、几只鸽子。

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 re-（回、再）加 place 构成，义为「放回原处；取代」
由前缀 dis-（离开）加 place 构成，义为「使离开原位；迫使迁移」

senses.title: A particular position or area
senses.definition: a particular position, area or spot, especially one used for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 某一个具体的位置、区域或地点，尤指有特定用途的地方
senses.example: This is a good place to stop for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这是个过夜的好地方。
senses.why: Latin platea named a broad open street, and an open surface is the first thing the eye can point at; from any open area the word narrowed to one particular spot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 platea 原指宽阔的露天街道，露天的面是最先能被指认的东西；词义于是从任意一片空地收窄为某一个具体地点。

senses.title: A seat or position kept for someone
senses.definition: a seat, space or position reserved for one person, as at a table or in a queue
senses.definitionCN: 在桌边或队伍里为某一个人留出的座位、空间或位置
senses.example: Please keep my place at the table while I get some water.
senses.exampleCN: 我去倒水的时候，请帮我留着桌边的位子。
senses.why: Once a wide surface can be divided among the people standing on it, a share of that surface can be held for one person, and place comes to mean a reserved seat.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的场地一旦被站在上面的人划分开来，其中一份就能为某个人留着，place 因此有了「预留座位」的意思。

senses.title: A rank in a competition
senses.definition: the position someone finishes in a race or competition, counted from the winner
senses.definitionCN: 某人在赛跑或比赛中到达终点的位次，从冠军开始数
senses.example: Our team finished in second place.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队获得了第二名。
senses.why: A race turns open ground into a line of positions, and the order in which runners reach the finish gives each one a place in the ranking.
senses.whyCN: 赛跑把开阔的场地变成一排有先后的位置，跑者到达终点的次序就给每个人定下了名次。

senses.title: To put something in a position
senses.definition: to put something in a particular position, or to arrange it there deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在某个特定位置，或有意把它安排在那里
senses.example: He placed the vase carefully on the windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心地把花瓶放在窗台上。
senses.why: The verb comes straight from the noun: to place an object is to give it the spot that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接从名词而来：place 一样东西，就是给它一个名词所指的位置。

intro.en: Place goes back to a Greek word for a broad way, which Latin borrowed for a wide street and French narrowed to an open square and then to any spot.
intro.cn: place 上溯到希腊语中表示「宽阔道路」的词，拉丁语借来指宽街，法语把它收窄为开阔的广场，再收窄为任何一个地点。

items.en: Greek plateia, short for plateia hodos, meant a broad way, and it was built on platys, broad.
items.cn: 希腊语 plateia 是 plateia hodos 的省略，意为宽阔的道路，建立在 platys（宽的）之上。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as platea, a broad street or an open court.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词借作 platea，指宽阔的街道或露天的庭院。

items.en: Old French place named an open space or square in a town, and also a spot or a position.
items.cn: 古法语 place 指城镇里的空地、广场，也指某个地点或位置。

items.en: Middle English place covered open ground, a spot, and a person's rank or standing.
items.cn: 中古英语的 place 兼指空地、地点，以及一个人的身份地位。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spot, adds the reserved seat and the finishing rank, and uses place as a verb of putting.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「地点」，加上预留座位与比赛名次，并让 place 作动词表示放置。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for a broad open space and three words that merely share its letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for a position or a site.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示开阔场地的拉丁词展开，另收三个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示位置与地点的词。

entries.definition: A public square or market area; Spanish kept the Latin word for a broad open space.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场或集市空地；西班牙语保留了拉丁语里表示开阔场地的这个词。

entries.definition: A flat dish or sheet; it looks like place but comes from another Romance word for something flat, so the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 平盘或平板；拼写与 place 相近，却来自另一个表示扁平物的罗曼语词，词源不同。

entries.definition: A raised area of flat land; the resemblance is in spelling only, and the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 高原；只是拼写相像，来源不同。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, is behind it, not the root of place.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），并非 place 的词根。

entries.definition: A particular place where something is or happens.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所在或某事发生的特定地方。

entries.definition: A small area or a particular point on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块地方，或表面上某个具体的点。

entries.definition: The place where someone or something is, or a rank in an order.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物所在的位置，也指次序中的名次。

entries.definition: A place where a building stands or where an event happened.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑所在或事件发生的地点。

normalIntro.en: The word began as open ground that anyone could point at, and its family keeps three pictures: a square, a spot held for someone, and a numbered position.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从谁都能指出的开阔场地开始，词族里保留着三幅画面：广场、为某人留着的位置，以及编了号的位次。

normal.en: Greek plateia meant a broad way, and Latin platea kept that open street, so the oldest picture is a wide surface underfoot.
normal.cn: 希腊语 plateia 意为宽阔的道路，拉丁语 platea 保留了这条开阔的街，所以最古老的画面是脚下的一大片地面。

normal.en: Old French place already meant both a town square and a spot, and English kept both, which is why a public square and a seat can share the word.
normal.cn: 古法语 place 已经同时指城镇广场和某个地点，英语两者都保留，所以广场和座位能共用一个词。

normal.en: Replace is re- plus place, to put back; displace is dis- plus place, to drive something away from its place.
normal.cn: replace 是 re- 加 place，表示放回；displace 是 dis- 加 place，表示把东西赶离原位。

normal.en: Take place means happen, because an event takes its spot in time the way an object takes its spot on the ground.
normal.cn: take place 意为发生，因为一件事像物体占地一样，在时间里占住自己的位置。

normal.en: The verb is regular: places, placed, placing, and the silent e is dropped before -ing.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：places、placed、placing，词尾不发音的 e 在 -ing 前去掉。

abstract.en: A place is not a thing but a promise that a thing can be found there.
abstract.cn: 地点本身不是东西，而是一个承诺：在那里能找到某样东西。

abstract.en: To hold a place for someone is to turn empty space into a small piece of waiting.
abstract.cn: 为某人留一个位置，就是把空地变成一小块等待。

abstract.en: First place and last place describe the same track; only the order of arrival makes the difference.
abstract.cn: 第一名和最后一名描述的是同一条跑道，区别只在到达的先后。

examples.en: This is a good place to stop for the night.
examples.cn: 这是个过夜的好地方。

examples.en: Our team finished in second place.
examples.cn: 我们队获得了第二名。

examples.en: He placed the vase carefully on the windowsill.
examples.cn: 他小心地把花瓶放在窗台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺来石」——地上铺来石板，就成了一个地方；记住 place 是地方。

root: 希腊语 plateia（宽阔的道路）经拉丁语 platea（宽街、露天庭院）与古法语 place（广场、地点）进入英语；西班牙语 plaza 保留了同一个拉丁词「开阔场地」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open surface that can be pointed at; the senses run from a particular spot, to a seat reserved for one person, to a rank in a race, and finally to the act of putting something there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一片能被指认的开阔地面；义项从具体地点，走到为某人留的座位，再到比赛名次，最后落到把东西放到那里这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear patch of stone in the middle of a busy square.
core.cn: 核心意象：热闹广场中央一块干净的石板地。

branches.en: an empty market square at midday
branches.cn: 正午空下来的集市广场

branches.en: a chair pulled out for a guest at the table
branches.cn: 为客人拉开的椅子

branches.en: a coat on a chair keeping a seat for someone
branches.cn: 搭在椅上替人占位的外套

branches.en: a runner crossing the line second
branches.cn: 第二个冲过终点的跑者

branches.en: a vase set down on a windowsill
branches.cn: 搁在窗台上的花瓶

intro.en: The word is a Romance borrowing built on a Greek adjective for broad, and English prefixes and suffixes then turn it into verbs and a noun of arrangement.
intro.cn: 这个词是罗曼语借词，建立在表示「宽阔」的希腊形容词上，英语的前缀与后缀随后把它变成动词和一个表示安置的名词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin noun is recorded behind this word: platea, the broad street that Greek supplied and French later narrowed to a square.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有一个可考的拉丁名词 platea，即希腊语提供、后来被法语收窄为广场的那条宽街。

items.meaning: to put back or take the place of
to move out of its position
the act of putting in position

definition_zh: 计划；打算；平面图；设计
definition_en: an organized idea of what will be done; a drawing of a building or area seen from above; to arrange something in advance; and to design a building or a town
core_image: 一张摊开的纸上，铅笔先画出方框，再写满步骤
scene: 铺开的图纸压住桌角，铅笔在方格之间来回比量。The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 plan 是「计划、方案」（第 1 个义项：事先安排好的做法）；句意为议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。图中可辨识物件：图纸、铅笔、方格线。

derivatives.zh: 由 plan 双写末尾的 n 再加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「计划者；规划师」
由 plan 加 -ing 构成，义为「规划；计划工作」
由否定前缀 un- 加 planned 构成，义为「未计划的；意外的」

senses.title: An organized idea of what will be done
senses.definition: an organized set of steps or intentions for doing something in the future
senses.definitionCN: 为将来做某事而安排好的步骤或意图
senses.example: The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。
senses.why: The word first named a flat drawing, and a scheme is laid out on paper the way a building is drawn from above, so the flat sheet became the shape of future action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一张平面图，而方案也是像俯视建筑那样铺在纸上的，于是平坦的纸面变成了未来行动的轮廓。

senses.title: A drawing of a building seen from above
senses.definition: a drawing that shows the shape and arrangement of rooms, roads or land as if seen from directly above
senses.definitionCN: 像从正上方俯视那样，画出一座建筑、一片街区或一块土地的布局
senses.example: The architect spread the plan across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师把平面图摊在桌上。
senses.why: Because Latin planum meant a flat surface, the drawing of a floor laid out flat is the oldest physical sense, and it still names what builders work from.
senses.whyCN: 因为拉丁语 planum 意为平坦的面，把楼层平铺画出来就是最古老的实物义，至今仍指施工所依据的那张图。

senses.title: To arrange something in advance
senses.definition: to decide and arrange in advance what one will do or how something will be done
senses.definitionCN: 事先决定并安排好要做什么或怎样做
senses.example: We plan to leave before the traffic builds up.
senses.exampleCN: 我们打算在车流变多之前出发。
senses.why: The verb turns the sheet of intentions into an activity: to plan is to keep laying out the steps the way the drawing lays out the rooms.
senses.whyCN: 动词把那纸意图变成一种活动：plan 就是像图上铺开房间那样，不断把步骤铺排出来。

senses.title: To design a building or a town
senses.definition: to design the layout of a building, a district or a town
senses.definitionCN: 设计一座建筑、一片街区或一座城镇的布局
senses.example: The whole district was planned around a central square.
senses.exampleCN: 整个街区都是围绕一个中央广场规划出来的。
senses.why: When the flat drawing is put to work on real ground, the same word moves from describing a layout to deciding it.
senses.whyCN: 当那张平面图被用到真实的地面上，同一个词就从「描画布局」变成「决定布局」。

intro.en: Plan comes from Latin planus, flat, and planum, a flat surface; the flat drawing gave French and then English the word for a scheme.
intro.cn: plan 来自拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）；正是这张平铺的图，把「方案」这个意思给了法语，再给了英语。

items.en: Planus meant flat, level or even, and it described ground that had no bumps in it.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的、齐平的，用来形容没有起伏的地面。

items.en: The noun planum named a flat surface or level ground, and from it came the idea of a drawing laid out flat.
items.cn: 名词 planum 指平坦的表面或平地，由此生出「平铺开来的图」这一想法。

items.en: French plan used the word for a ground plan, the flat drawing of a building or a camp seen from above.
items.cn: 法语 plan 用这个词指平面图，即从上方俯视建筑或营地的平铺图。

items.en: English borrowed plan for such a drawing and soon extended it to any arranged scheme of action.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 plan 指这类图纸，很快又扩展到任何安排好的行动方案。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawing, the scheme and the verb of intending, and adds planned towns and planned economies.
items.cn: 现代英语保留图纸、方案与表示打算的动词，并加上规划城镇、计划经济这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for flat, plus two that only share letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for a scheme or a schedule.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「平」这个形容词上的词，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示方案与日程的词。

entries.definition: Flat and open, or simple; it comes from the same Latin adjective for level ground.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦开阔的，或朴素的；来自同一个表示平地的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: In its flat-surface senses this word shares the Latin root planus, though its aircraft sense has another source.
entries.definitionCN: 在「平面」这些义项上与本词共享拉丁词根 planus，不过它的「飞机」义另有来源。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, lies behind it, so the resemblance is spelling alone.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），只是拼写相像。

entries.definition: A living thing that grows in soil; the source is Latin planta, a sprout or a sole, not planus.
entries.definitionCN: 在土里生长的生物；来源是拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），并不是 planus，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A large or slightly secret plan for achieving something.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成某事而设计的大计划或略带隐秘的安排。

entries.definition: A planned piece of work with a clear aim.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确目标的计划性工作。

entries.definition: A list or timetable of things to be done at set times.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定时间安排事务的清单或时间表。

entries.definition: A drawing or arrangement showing how something will be made.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物如何制作的图样或安排。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin adjective for flat, and the whole family keeps the picture of something laid out on a level sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「平」的形容词上，整族词都带着「铺在平整纸面上」的画面。

normal.en: Latin planus means flat, so a plan began as a flat drawing rather than a thought in the head.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为平的，所以 plan 最初是一张平铺的图，而不是脑子里的念头。

normal.en: A floor plan is the oldest kind of plan, and it still means a view of a building from directly above.
normal.cn: floor plan 是最古老的一种 plan，至今仍指从正上方俯视建筑所得的图。

normal.en: The verb doubles the final n: planned and planning, to keep the short vowel of plan.
normal.cn: 动词变化时末尾的 n 双写：planned、planning，以保持 plan 的短元音。

normal.en: Planner adds -er to the stem and names the person, while planning names the activity.
normal.cn: planner 在词干后加 -er 指人，planning 则指这项活动。

normal.en: According to plan means everything is going the way the sheet said it would.
normal.cn: according to plan 意为一切都按那张纸所写的那样进行。

abstract.en: A plan is a flat drawing of time, with rooms replaced by steps.
abstract.cn: 计划是一张关于时间的平面图，把房间换成了步骤。

abstract.en: To plan ahead is to trust that a sheet of paper can stand in for a stretch of the future.
abstract.cn: 提前计划，就是相信一张纸能够代替一段尚未到来的时间。

abstract.en: The same word draws a building and decides a life, because both begin as lines on a level surface.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既画建筑也安排人生，因为两者都从平整面上的一堆线开始。

examples.en: The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
examples.cn: 议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。

examples.en: We plan to leave before the traffic builds up.
examples.cn: 我们打算在车流变多之前出发。

examples.en: The whole district was planned around a central square.
examples.cn: 整个街区都是围绕一个中央广场规划出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺烂」——图纸铺烂了也要把方案画完；记住 plan 是计划。

root: 拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）经法语 plan（平面图）进入英语：先指俯视的图纸，再指事先安排好的方案。plant 与 plantation 来自另一个拉丁词 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），与 plan 只是拼写相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a layout drawn on a flat surface; the senses run from the drawing of a building, to a scheme of action, to intending, and finally to designing a district.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是画在平面上的布局；义项从建筑图纸，走到行动方案，再到打算，最后落到规划一片街区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil tracing rooms on a sheet laid flat, then writing steps in the same frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔在摊平的纸上勾出房间，又在同样的方框里写下步骤。

branches.en: a list of steps pinned above a desk
branches.cn: 钉在书桌上方的步骤清单

branches.en: a floor plan spread under a pencil
branches.cn: 铅笔下摊开的平面图

branches.en: a drawing turning into a timetable
branches.cn: 图纸变成时间表

branches.en: two people agreeing when to leave
branches.cn: 两个人商量什么时候出发

branches.en: streets laid out around one square
branches.cn: 围绕一个广场铺开的街道

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of flatness turned into a French noun of drawing, and English adds the usual endings for people and activities.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词，变成法语里表示图纸的名词，英语又给它加上表示人与活动的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin forms are recorded behind this word: the adjective planus, flat, and the noun planum, a flat surface.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有两个可考的拉丁形式：形容词 planus（平的）与名词 planum（平面）。

definition_zh: 飞机；平面；层面；刨子；平的
definition_en: an aircraft with wings and engines; a flat surface in geometry; a level of thought or existence; a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood; and flat or level
core_image: 跑道上银色的机翼，映出远处一块平整的水泥地
scene: 跑道尽头的灯一盏盏亮起，机翼在风里轻轻发抖。The plane lifted off the runway just as the sun cleared the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 plane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：有翼有动力的航空器）；句意为太阳刚越过山脊，飞机就离开了跑道。图中可辨识物件：跑道灯、机翼、远处的山脊。

derivatives.zh: 由 plane 加形容词后缀 -ar 构成，义为「平面的」
由希腊语 aero-（空气）与 plane 复合而成，义为「飞机」（英式拼写）
由 plane 加表示工具或人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「刨床；刨工」

senses.title: An aircraft with wings and engines
senses.definition: a vehicle with wings and one or more engines that flies through the air
senses.definitionCN: 有翼、带一台或多台发动机、在空中飞行的交通工具
senses.example: Our plane was delayed by two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的飞机晚点了两个小时。
senses.why: This sense is a twentieth-century shortening of aeroplane, a French word built from Greek aer, air, and planer, to soar; the flat-surface word simply took over the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪对 aeroplane 的缩略，那个法语词由希腊语 aer（空气）与 planer（翱翔）构成；它只是借用了表示「平面」那个词的拼写。

senses.title: A flat surface in geometry
senses.definition: a completely flat surface such that a straight line joining any two of its points lies wholly within it
senses.definitionCN: 完全平坦的面，面上任意两点连成的直线都整条落在该面内
senses.example: A plane has length and width but no thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 平面有长和宽，却没有厚度。
senses.why: Latin planum named level ground, and geometers took the same word for the perfectly even surface that ground only approximates.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 planum 指平地，几何学家借用同一个词，指地面只能近似达到的那种绝对平整的面。

senses.title: A level of thought or existence
senses.definition: a level on which ideas, activities or kinds of existence are considered to operate
senses.definitionCN: 思想、活动或存在方式被认为所处的某一层次
senses.example: Their argument moved onto a more practical plane.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争论转到了一个更实际的层面上。
senses.why: Once a plane is an even surface, two things can sit on different surfaces without touching, so the word comes to name separate levels of experience.
senses.whyCN: 平面一旦成为一层平整的面，两样东西就能各处在不同的面上而互不接触，于是这个词也用来指经验中彼此分开的层次。

senses.title: A carpenter's tool for smoothing wood
senses.definition: a tool with a blade set in a block, pushed along wood to shave off thin layers and make it smooth
senses.definitionCN: 刀片装在木块里、沿木料推过以削去薄层使其平滑的工具
senses.example: He smoothed the edge of the board with a plane.
senses.exampleCN: 他用刨子把木板边缘刨平。
senses.why: The tool is named for the result it produces: a plane makes a surface flat, and the flat surface and the tool share one word in Latin and French.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具因它做出的结果得名：刨子把表面弄平，而「平面」与「工具」在拉丁语和法语里本来就共用一个词。

intro.en: Two different histories meet in one spelling: the flat surface and the woodworking tool come from Latin planus, while the aircraft is a shortened French coinage built on Greek aer.
intro.cn: 两种不同的来历汇成同一个拼写：平面与木工工具来自拉丁语 planus，而飞机则是对一个以希腊语 aer 造出的法语词的缩略。

items.en: Planus meant flat or level, and the noun planum named a flat surface or even ground.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的，名词 planum 指平面或平地。

items.en: Late Latin plana named a smoothing tool, and French plane kept that name for the carpenter's plane.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 plana 指一种弄平木料的工具，法语 plane 保留了这个名字，用来指木刨。

items.en: French aéroplane joined Greek aer, air, with planer, to soar or glide, and named a flying machine.
items.cn: 法语 aéroplane 把希腊语 aer（空气）与 planer（翱翔、滑翔）拼在一起，用来指飞行器。

items.en: English borrowed aeroplane and then clipped it to plane, so the aircraft inherited the spelling of the flat word.
items.cn: 英语借入 aeroplane，随后缩略为 plane，飞机就这样继承了那个表示「平」的词的拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps all four senses, but plane is not related to plant or plantation, which go back to Latin planta, a sprout or a sole.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了四个义项；但 plane 与 plant、plantation 无关，后两者上溯到拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌）。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin flat family and two words that only share letters; the near-meaning group gathers aircraft and words for a flat level.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「平」这一族词，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收航空器与表示平面层次的词。

entries.definition: Flat and open, or simple; it comes from the same Latin adjective for level ground.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦开阔的，或朴素的；来自同一个表示平地的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: A scheme or a ground drawing; it shares the Latin root planus with the flat senses of plane.
entries.definitionCN: 方案或平面图；在「平面」这些义项上与本词共享拉丁词根 planus。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, lies behind it, so the likeness is spelling alone.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），只是拼写相像。

entries.definition: A living thing that grows in soil; it comes from Latin planta, a sprout or a sole, not from planus, so the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 在土里生长的生物；来自拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），并非 planus，与此词词源不同。

entries.definition: Any vehicle that flies, including planes and helicopters.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能飞的交通工具，包括飞机与直升机。

entries.definition: A fast plane driven by jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的快速飞机。

entries.definition: A height or a standard, or a flat position.
entries.definitionCN: 高度、水准，或平坦的位置。

entries.definition: The outer or top layer of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外层或表面。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two stories in one spelling: a Latin adjective for flat gave the surface and the tool, while a French word for soaring gave the aircraft.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词用同一个拼写装着两个故事：拉丁语表示「平」的形容词给出平面与工具，法语中表示翱翔的词则给出飞机。

normal.en: Latin planus means flat, so the geometric plane and the smoothing tool both start from an even surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为平的，所以几何平面与刨平工具都从平整的面开始。

normal.en: The carpenter's plane is named for what it makes: a flat surface, the same idea as planum.
normal.cn: 木刨因它做出的结果得名：一个平整的面，和 planum 是同一个念头。

normal.en: The aircraft sense is a clipping of aeroplane, where aero- means air and planer means to soar.
normal.cn: 飞机这个义项是 aeroplane 的缩略，其中 aero- 意为空气，planer 意为翱翔。

normal.en: Plane is not related to plant: plant and plantation go back to Latin planta, a sprout or a sole of the foot.
normal.cn: plane 与 plant 无关：plant 与 plantation 上溯到拉丁语 planta，意为嫩芽或脚掌。

normal.en: Planar adds -ar and means lying in a plane, while planer adds -er and names the tool or the worker.
normal.cn: planar 加 -ar，意为位于一个平面内；planer 加 -er，指工具或刨工。

abstract.en: A word can wear one spelling while carrying two unrelated pasts, like two travellers sharing a coat.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以用同一个拼写背着两段互不相干的过去，就像两个旅人共用一件外套。

abstract.en: To smooth a board and to cross an ocean both aim at a surface that will not tilt.
abstract.cn: 刨平一块木板与飞越一片海洋，追求的都是一个不会倾斜的面。

abstract.en: A different plane of thought is simply a surface the other person is not standing on.
abstract.cn: 所谓另一个思维层面，不过是对方没有站在上面的那块面。

examples.en: Our plane was delayed by two hours.
examples.cn: 我们的飞机晚点了两个小时。

examples.en: A plane has length and width but no thickness.
examples.cn: 平面有长和宽，却没有厚度。

examples.en: He smoothed the edge of the board with a plane.
examples.cn: 他用刨子把木板边缘刨平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱」——飞机扑棱着翅膀上了天；记住 plane 是飞机。

root: plane 有两套来历：平面、刨子来自拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）；飞机义则是 aeroplane 的缩略，来自希腊语 aer（空气）加法语 planer（翱翔）。plane 与 plant 不同源，plant 与 plantation 才同出拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an even surface; the senses run from the geometric plane, to a level of thought, to the tool that makes wood even, and to the aircraft that took the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个平整的面；义项从几何平面，走到思维层面，再到把木头弄平的工具，最后是借用了这个拼写的飞机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver wing over level concrete, and a plane shaving a curl from a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：平整的水泥地上方掠过银色机翼，刨子从木板上卷起一层薄花。

branches.cn: 机翼在跑道灯上方倾斜

branches.en: a line lying wholly inside one flat sheet
branches.cn: 整条落在同一平面内的直线

branches.en: two people talking past each other on different levels

branches.cn: 刨刃卷起的一层木花

intro.en: One half of the word is a Latin adjective of flatness with its tool noun; the other half is a Greek prefix of air joined to a French verb of soaring.
intro.cn: 这个词的一半是拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词及其工具名词；另一半是希腊语中表示「空气」的前缀加上法语中表示「翱翔」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for the flat and tool senses: the adjective planus, the noun planum, and the late noun plana for a smoothing tool.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「平面」与「工具」的义项有可考的拉丁形式：形容词 planus、名词 planum，以及晚期拉丁语中指弄平工具的名词 plana。

senses.title: The IAU definition
senses.titleCN: 天文学定义：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道
senses.definition: a body that orbits the sun or another star, is massive enough to be nearly round, and has cleared its neighbourhood of comparable bodies
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳或其他恒星运行、质量足以近似球形，并已清空轨道附近同类天体的天体
senses.example: A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
senses.exampleCN: 目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。
senses.why: the definition was tightened in 2006 to separate planets from the many similar-sized bodies in belts, so three conditions replaced the older informal one.
senses.whyCN: 这一定义在 2006 年被收紧，以把行星与带中大量同样大小的天体区分开，于是三条条件取代了旧的松散说法。

senses.title: One of the eight
senses.definition: one of the eight bodies recognised in the solar system, from Mercury to Neptune
senses.definitionCN: 太阳系中公认的八颗天体之一，从水星到海王星
senses.example: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星。
senses.why: everyday use keeps the older, simpler list, so 'planet' usually means one of the eight even in careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法沿用更旧、更简单的名单，因此即使在谨慎的说法里，planet 通常也指八颗之一。

senses.title: A planet of another star
senses.titleCN: 其他恒星的行星（系外行星）
senses.definition: used with modifiers for bodies orbiting stars other than the sun
senses.definitionCN: 与修饰语连用，指绕太阳以外恒星运行的天体
senses.example: The telescope found a planet in a tight four-day orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜发现了一颗四天就绕一圈的行星。
senses.why: once other stars were known to have such bodies, the noun needed no new word; the modifier carries the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当其他恒星被确认拥有这类天体后，这个名词无需新词，差别由修饰语承担。

senses.title: Dwarf planet as a boundary case
senses.definition: used in the compound dwarf planet for a round body that has not cleared its neighbourhood, such as Pluto
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词「矮行星」，指近似球形但未清空轨道附近的天体，如冥王星
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星在 2006 年被改归为矮行星。
senses.why: the boundary had to be drawn somewhere, and the compound keeps the old word while marking the failed third condition.
senses.whyCN: 边界总得画在某处，而这个复合词保留了旧词，同时标出它未满足第三条条件。

senses.title: The earth as 'the planet'
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean the earth, especially in environmental talk
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时指地球，尤用于环境话题
senses.example: We treat the planet as if its resources had no limit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这颗行星当作资源没有上限。
senses.why: seen from outside, the earth is simply one planet, so the definite noun becomes a way of speaking about all of us at once.
senses.whyCN: 从外面看，地球只是一颗行星，因此这个带冠词的名词成了一种把所有人一起谈论的说法。

senses.title: Living on another planet
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.definition: in the phrase on another planet, describing someone out of touch with present reality
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「在另一颗行星上」，形容某人心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.example: His plan was elegant and completely on another planet.
senses.exampleCN: 他的方案很精巧，却完全不接地气。
senses.why: the image works because another planet is a place with different rules, so a person out of touch seems to live there.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象成立，是因为另一颗行星是一个规则不同的地方，脱离现实的人仿佛就住在那儿。

senses.title: Astrology's seven planets
senses.titleCN: 占星中的七行星（含日月）
senses.definition: in astrology, one of the seven traditional bodies: sun, moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn
senses.definitionCN: 占星中七颗传统天体之一：日、月、水星、金星、火星、木星与土星
senses.example: Old charts assign each planet a day of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 旧星盘为每颗行星分配一周中的一天。
senses.why: astrology preserves the ancient list in which the sun and moon also wandered, so its 'planets' are not the astronomer's.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了太阳与月亮也会游走的古老名单，因此它的「行星」并非天文学家的行星。

senses.title: The old wandering stars
senses.definition: historically, any of the lights that moved against the fixed stars, including the sun and moon
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指任何相对于恒星移动的光点，包括太阳与月亮
senses.example: Ancient observers counted seven planets, sun and moon included.
senses.exampleCN: 古代观测者数出七颗行星，日月也在其中。
senses.why: the word meant 'wanderer' before it meant 'world', so the older list follows the original meaning rather than the modern one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在指「世界」之前意为「漫游者」，因此旧的名单遵循原义而非今义。

senses.title: A world in fiction
senses.titleCN: 虚构作品中的「行星世界」
senses.definition: used in science fiction for a habitable or visited world with its own conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在科幻作品中指可居住或可造访、有自身条件的世界
senses.example: The crew landed on a planet where a day lasts a month.
senses.exampleCN: 船员降落在一颗一天长达一个月的行星上。
senses.why: stories need a unit of setting larger than a country and smaller than a galaxy, and the planet supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 故事需要一个大于国家、小于星系的设定单位，而行星恰好提供了它。

intro.en: Planet comes from Greek planētēs 'wanderer', through Latin planeta and Old French. The word meant a moving star long before it meant a world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planet 来自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」，经拉丁 planeta 与古法语进入英语。在它指「世界」之前，很久以来都指会移动的星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomers called the five moving lights planētēs, 'wanderers', because they drifted against the fixed stars.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家把五个移动的光点称作 planētēs「漫游者」，因为它们相对恒星漂移。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun as planeta and kept the meaning 'wandering star'; the sun and moon were often counted among them.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 planeta，保留「游星」之义；太阳与月亮常被算在其中。

items.en: Old French planete carried the word into English in the Middle Ages, still as an astronomical body rather than a world.
items.cn: 古法语 planete 在中世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指天文天体而非一个世界。

items.en: From the seventeenth century telescopes showed planets as disks and worlds, and the word shifted from 'moving light' to 'physical body'.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，望远镜让行星显出圆盘与世界的模样，这个词便从「移动的光」转为「实体天体」。

items.en: The International Astronomical Union fixed three conditions in 2006 and created the dwarf planet category for bodies that fail the third.
items.cn: 国际天文学联合会在 2006 年定下三条条件，并为未满足第三条的天体设立「矮行星」类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of planasthai 'to wander' is not established, and any older Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：planasthai「漫游」在希腊语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words derived from planet that name related bodies; group two holds sky objects that are often mistaken for planets.
note.cn: 第一组是由 planet 派生、指相关天体的词；第二组是常被误认作行星的天空对象。

entries.definition: The adjective of planet; it describes relations and systems rather than naming a body.
entries.definitionCN: planet 的形容词；描述关系与系统，而非命名天体。

entries.definition: A small body that looks like a planet but is not one; the -oid suffix marks resemblance, not membership.
entries.definitionCN: 形似行星而非行星的小天体；-oid 后缀标记相似而非归类。

entries.definition: One of the small bodies that collide and grow into planets; it is a stage, not a category of planet.
entries.definitionCN: 碰撞并长成行星的小天体之一；它是一个阶段，而非行星的一个类别。

entries.definition: Exo- 'outside' plus planet: a planet of a star other than the sun, so the head noun is still planet.
entries.definitionCN: exo-「在外」加 planet：太阳以外某颗恒星的行星，中心词仍是 planet。

entries.definition: A body that shines by its own fusion; planets only reflect light, which is why the two were once distinguished by motion.
entries.definitionCN: 靠自身核聚变发光的天体；行星只反射光，这正是两词最初靠运动来区分的原因。

entries.definition: A natural body orbiting a planet; a planet orbits a star, so the two words mark different centres.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行星运行的天然天体；行星绕恒星，因此两词标记不同的中心。

entries.definition: A place with its own conditions, often used for planets in fiction; it is a broader, older word.
entries.definitionCN: 有自身条件的地方，常用于虚构中的行星；是更宽、更古老的词。

entries.definition: The neutral word for any discrete object in space, used when the class is unknown or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中任何独立天体的中性词，用于类别未知或不重要时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real history, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实历史，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': planets were the lights that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的光点。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetoid, planetesimal, exoplanet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetoid、planetesimal、exoplanet。

normal.en: Three IAU conditions: orbit a star, be nearly round, clear the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 国际天文学联合会三条条件：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道附近。

normal.en: The eight are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
normal.cn: 八颗是水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星。

normal.en: Astrology still counts sun and moon among its seven planets.
normal.cn: 占星仍把太阳与月亮算在它的七颗行星中。

abstract.en: Picture a marble circling a lamp in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一颗弹珠绕着一盏灯转。

abstract.en: Picture a single room that must hold everyone's weather at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间必须同时装下所有人的天气。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who follows rules from a place nobody else can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按别人看不见的地方的规则行事的陌生人。

examples.en: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the sun.
examples.cn: 水星是最小的行星，也是离太阳最近的一颗。

examples.en: Planets form from the same disk of dust that makes their star.
examples.cn: 行星由构成其恒星的同一片尘埃盘形成。

examples.en: The probe will study the planet's thin atmosphere from orbit.
examples.cn: 探测器将在轨道上研究这颗行星的稀薄大气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内特（planet）」——天上到处乱跑的那颗球 → 行星

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」← planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta、古法语 planete 进入英语；今义经望远镜观测由「移动的光」转为「实体世界」。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the tightened definition, move to the eight, to other stars' planets and the dwarf boundary, then to the earth itself, a metaphor, astrology, the old list and fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项先从收紧后的定义开始，再到八颗行星、别的恒星的行星与矮行星边界，然后到地球本身、一个比喻、占星、旧名单与虚构作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one round body held in a path around a much larger light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个圆体被维持在一条绕更大光源的路径上。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND LIST: a strict rule and the familiar eight answer the same question at different depths.
branches.cn: 定义与名单：严格规则与熟悉的八颗在不同深度回答同一个问题。

branches.en: EDGES OF THE CLASS: other stars' planets and dwarf planets test where the word stops.
branches.cn: 类别的边缘：别恒星的行星与矮行星都在试探这个词的边界。

branches.en: ONE PLANET, TWO VIEWS: the earth as home, and a metaphor for being out of touch.
branches.cn: 一颗行星两种看法：作为家园的地球，以及脱离现实的比喻。

branches.en: OLD LISTS: astrology and ancient astronomy keep sun and moon inside the word.
branches.cn: 旧名单：占星与古代天文学把日月留在词内。

branches.en: STAGE OF A STORY: fiction uses the planet as its unit of setting.
branches.cn: 故事的舞台：虚构作品把行星当作设定单位。

intro.en: Planet is a Greek noun borrowed through Latin; English builds a large family from it with suffixes for relation, resemblance and size.
intro.cn: planet 是经拉丁借入的希腊名词；英语用表示关系、相似与大小的后缀从中构建了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta and the adjective planetarius carry the word; Latin also said stella errans 'wandering star' for the same object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta 与形容词 planetarius 承载这个词；拉丁也用 stella errans「游星」指同一对象。

items.exampleCN: 八大行星大小差异极大。

items.example: Planetary science grew from telescope work.
items.exampleCN: 行星科学由望远镜工作发展而来。

items.example: The planetoid orbits between Mars and Jupiter.
items.exampleCN: 这个小行星体在火星与木星之间运行。

items.example: Planetesimals stuck together in the early disk.
items.exampleCN: 早期盘中星子粘合在一起。

items.exampleCN: 现已知道数千颗系外行星。

senses.title: A synthetic mouldable material
senses.definition: a light artificial material made from chemicals, used to make bottles, bags and countless objects
senses.definitionCN: 用化学原料制成的轻质人造材料，用来做瓶子、袋子等大量物品
senses.example: Most of the bottles in the fridge are made of plastic.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里大多数瓶子都是塑料做的。
senses.why: Greek plastikos described anything fit for moulding, so when chemists found a material that could be poured into a shape and set, the old word for mouldable was ready to name it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 plastikos 指「适合被塑造的」，所以当化学家找到一种可以浇进模子再定型的材料时，这个古老的「可塑」之词正好拿来命名它。

senses.title: Made of plastic
senses.definition: made of plastic rather than metal, glass or wood
senses.definitionCN: 用塑料而非金属、玻璃或木头制成的
senses.example: She packed the sandwiches in a plastic box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三明治装在一个塑料盒里。
senses.why: Once the noun named the material, the same form could stand in front of another noun as an adjective, simply marking what the thing is made of.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指认了这种材料，同一个词形就能站到另一个名词前面作形容词，只标示这件东西是用什么做的。

senses.title: Easily shaped or influenced
senses.definition: soft enough to be shaped, or figuratively easy to influence and change
senses.definitionCN: 软到可以被塑造，也可比喻容易受影响、被改变
senses.example: Young minds are plastic and quick to absorb new habits.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的心智可塑性强，能很快吸收新习惯。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the material sense grew out of it. Anything plastic takes an impression from outside and keeps it, which is why the word also describes a mind that can still be moulded.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，物质义正是从它长出来的。凡是可塑的东西都会留下外来的印记并保持住，所以这个词也能形容一颗仍可被塑造的心。

senses.title: Repairing the body by surgery
senses.definition: connected with surgery that repairs or reshapes damaged or unwanted parts of the body
senses.definitionCN: 与修复或重塑身体受损部位、不满意部位的外科手术有关
senses.example: The burn left a scar that plastic surgery could soften.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤留下的疤可以通过整形手术淡化。
senses.why: Doctors who rebuilt damaged faces spoke of plastic surgery because they were literally reshaping tissue, borrowing the moulding image rather than the material one.
senses.whyCN: 重建受损面孔的医生把这类手术叫作整形外科，因为他们确实在重塑组织，用的是「塑造」的意象，而非「塑料」这种材料。

intro.en: Plastic comes from a Greek word for moulding, entered English through Latin and French, and only later became the name of a material.
intro.cn: plastic 出自希腊语中表示「塑造」的词，经拉丁语和法语进入英语，很久以后才成为某种材料的名字。

items.en: The verb plassein meant to mould clay or form a shape with the hands.
items.cn: 动词 plassein 意为捏塑黏土或用双手做出形状。

items.en: The adjective plastikos described what could be moulded, especially the art of the modeller.
items.cn: 形容词 plastikos 形容可以被塑造的东西，尤其指塑形这门手艺。

items.en: Latin took plasticus from Greek as a learned adjective; it is generally treated as a borrowing rather than a native Latin root.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 plasticus 是从希腊语借来的学术形容词，而非拉丁本土词根。

items.en: French plastique carried both the moulding sense and, from the nineteenth century, the sense of a material that can be pressed into shape.
items.cn: 法语 plastique 既保留「塑造」义，也从十九世纪起指可以被压制成型的材料。

items.en: English plastic first meant mouldable, then named the cheap synthetic material of the twentieth century, and widened again to surgery and to flexible minds.
items.cn: 英语 plastic 先指「可塑的」，随后指二十世纪廉价的人造材料，又扩展到整形手术与灵活的心智。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a comment on how easily something takes a shape, and that image still sits under the material, the adjective and the surgery.

normal.cn: 希腊语 plassein 意为捏塑，所以 plastic 字面就是「能被塑形的东西」。

normal.en: Plasticity keeps the old adjective stem and adds -ity, naming the quality itself.
normal.cn: plasticity 保留旧的形容词词干并加 -ity，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: A plastic bag is named for its material; a plastic smile is named for its fakeness, the same word pointing at two different judgments.
normal.cn: 塑料袋按材料命名，plastic smile 却按虚假命名，同一个词指向两种不同的判断。

normal.en: Plastic surgery reshapes tissue, so the moulding image survives even where no plastic is used.
normal.cn: 整形手术是在重塑组织，所以即便不用塑料，「塑造」的画面仍然在。

normal.en: Plaster looks close but comes from a different Greek word for a salve, so do not read it as a relative.
normal.cn: plaster 看着像，却出自另一个表示药膏的希腊词，不能当成同族词。

abstract.en: A material named after mouldability is a reminder that a word can describe a possibility before it describes a thing.
abstract.cn: 一种以「可塑性」命名的材料提醒人：词可以先描述一种可能性，再描述一件实物。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers a bottle and a smile, which shows how easily English lets a physical quality slide into a moral one.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既形容瓶子又形容笑容，说明英语很轻易就让物理性质滑向道德评价。

abstract.en: If something is plastic, it is not yet finished; the word quietly suggests that being shapeable is also being open.
abstract.cn: 说某物可塑，意味着它尚未定型；这个词悄悄暗示，能被塑造也意味着保持开放。

definition_zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者
definition_en: someone who takes part in a game or sport; also a device that plays recorded sound, a musician, or an active participant in a situation
core_image: 一个人站在场地中央，脚下有球，身后是等着看他下一步动作的观众
scene: 球场的看台渐渐坐满，替补席上有人不停活动脚踝。The coach waved the young player onto the field in the final minutes.
sceneCN: 这里是「运动员、球员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为教练在最后几分钟挥手让这名年轻球员上场。图中可辨识物件：替补席、边线、球鞋。

pos.zh: 运动员；播放器；演奏者；参与者

derivatives.zh: player 的基础动词，义为「玩；比赛；播放」
由 play 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「爱玩的；戏谑的」
由 play 与 off 复合而成，义为「附加赛；季后赛」

senses.title: Someone who plays a sport or game
senses.definition: a person who takes part in a sport or a game, especially as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育运动或比赛的人，尤指以此为职业者
senses.example: Their best player was injured in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最好的球员在上半场受伤了。
senses.why: The suffix -er simply marks the person who does the verb, so a player is first of all one who plays, whether on a field or at a table.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 只标示做这个动作的人，所以 player 首先是「玩的人」，无论在球场上还是在牌桌旁。

senses.title: A device that reproduces sound or video
senses.definition: a machine or program that plays recorded music, films or files
senses.definitionCN: 播放录音、影片或文件的机器或程序
senses.example: He put the disc into the player and turned up the volume.
senses.exampleCN: 他把光盘放进播放器，调高了音量。
senses.why: When machines took over the act of playing music, the same person-suffix was attached to the device, as if the machine now did the playing.
senses.whyCN: 当机器接手「播放音乐」这个动作时，同一个表人的后缀被安到了机器上，仿佛现在由机器来扮演这个角色。

senses.title: A musician
senses.definition: a person who plays a musical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 演奏乐器的人
senses.example: She is a fine player of the cello.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的大提琴演奏者。
senses.why: Long before recordings, the one who played was a person with an instrument in hand, and this sense keeps the word close to the body and the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 在有录音之前，演奏的人就是手持乐器的人，这个义项让词始终贴近身体与手指。

senses.title: An active participant in a situation
senses.definition: a person or group that takes an active part in an activity, market or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 积极介入某项活动、市场或谈判的人或团体
senses.example: The union is now a major player in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 工会如今是谈判中的重要一方。
senses.why: From a game, the word widens to any contest of interests: whoever can make a move and change the outcome deserves to be called a player.
senses.whyCN: 从游戏出发，这个词扩展到任何利益博弈：谁能出手并改变结局，谁就配得上 player 这个称呼。

intro.en: Player is the plain English agent noun of play; the verb itself is old and its deeper origin is usually described as uncertain.
intro.cn: player 是 play 的英语施事名词，构词十分直接；动词 play 本身很古老，更早的来源一般被认为不确定。

items.en: The verb plegian meant to exercise, frolic or take part in a game.
items.cn: 动词 plegian 意为活动身体、嬉戏或参加游戏。

items.en: The related noun plega named a game, sport or quick movement.
items.cn: 相关名词 plega 指游戏、运动或轻快的动作。

items.en: Middle English play kept the sense of sport and amusement and began to cover music and performance.
items.cn: 中古英语 play 保留运动与娱乐义，并开始涵盖音乐与表演。

items.en: The native suffix -er, meaning one who does, made player out of play in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 本土后缀 -er 表示「做某事的人」，在中古英语时期把 play 变成了 player。

items.en: Modern English extends player to machines that reproduce sound and to anyone with a stake in a contest.
items.cn: 现代英语把 player 扩展到播放声音的机器，以及任何在一场较量中有份的人。

note.cn: 形近组收 play 词族，以及一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表演、竞争或参与的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is play plus the person suffix, and every sense still asks the same question: who or what is doing the playing here?
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 play 加表人的后缀，每个义项都仍在问同一个问题：此刻是谁、是什么在「玩」？

normal.en: Player is play plus -er, the suffix for the one who does the action.
normal.cn: player 就是 play 加 -er，即「做这个动作的人」。

normal.en: A record player is a machine doing what a person used to do: playing the music.
normal.cn: 电唱机是一台机器在做过去由人做的事：播放音乐。

normal.en: A team player is not on the field but in the office: the image of a game is borrowed for cooperation.
normal.cn: team player 不在球场上而在办公室里：借用了比赛的画面来形容合作。

normal.en: Playful adds -ful, full of play, which shows how the family grows by short native suffixes.
normal.cn: playful 加 -ful，意为「充满玩的」，可见这个词族靠简短的本土后缀生长。

normal.en: Prayer is close in sound only; it comes from a Latin verb for begging and is not a relative.
normal.cn: prayer 只是读音相近，出自拉丁语中表示乞求的动词，并非同族词。

abstract.en: A word made by adding a person to an action reminds us that English often names a role before it names a thing.
abstract.cn: 给动作加上一个人，就造出一个词，这提醒人：英语常常先命名角色，再命名事物。

abstract.en: Calling a negotiator a player quietly turns a meeting into a game with moves and stakes.
abstract.cn: 把谈判者称作 player，悄悄把一场会议变成有招法、有输赢的游戏。

abstract.en: If a machine can be a player, then the word is less about being human than about taking the active part.
abstract.cn: 如果机器也能是 player，那么这个词的关键就不在于是不是人，而在于是否承担那个主动的角色。

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的
definition_en: giving pleasure to the senses or the mind; also friendly in manner, or agreeable as an experience
core_image: 推开门的一瞬间，暖风、光线和淡淡香气一起涌上来，人不由自主放松了肩膀
scene: 午后的花园里风很轻，桌上刚切开的柠檬散出清香。The garden felt pleasant in the soft afternoon light.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人愉快的、宜人的」（第 1 个义项）；句意为在柔和的午后光线里，这座花园让人感到惬意。图中可辨识物件：柠檬、白桌布、树影。

pos.zh: 令人愉快的；和善的；合意的

derivatives.zh: pleasant 的同源动词，义为「使高兴；请」
由 please 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「愉快；乐事」
由 pleasant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pleasant 构成，义为「令人不快的」

senses.title: Giving pleasure to the senses
senses.definition: giving a feeling of enjoyment to the senses, as a place, smell, sound or taste does
senses.definitionCN: 让感官产生愉悦，如地方、气味、声音或味道带来的舒服感
senses.example: The room was small but pleasant, with wide windows and warm light.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大却很宜人，窗户宽大，光线温暖。
senses.why: The word began as the present participle of the verb to please, so anything pleasant is literally something that is pleasing you while you experience it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是动词 please 的现在分词，所以凡是 pleasant 的东西，字面上就是正在让你愉悦的东西。

senses.title: Friendly and agreeable in manner
senses.definition: kind, polite and easy to be with, said of a person or a person's manner
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或其举止亲切、有礼、好相处
senses.example: Our host gave us a pleasant smile and showed us to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 主人朝我们和善地一笑，把我们引到桌边。
senses.why: If a thing can please, a person can please too; the adjective then moves from the effect on the senses to the social warmth of someone's behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 既然事物能使人愉悦，人也能使人愉悦；于是这个形容词从感官效果转到某人举止带来的社交暖意。

senses.title: Agreeable to the mind
senses.definition: satisfying or welcome as a piece of news, a task or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指消息、任务或安排令人满意、受欢迎
senses.example: It was a pleasant change to finish work before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天没黑就干完活，这种改变让人舒心。
senses.why: Beyond the senses lies the mind: what fits our plans and leaves us easy is also called pleasant, which shows how far the pleasing image can reach.
senses.whyCN: 感官之外还有心智：合乎计划、让人安心的事也被称作 pleasant，可见「使人愉悦」这幅画面能延伸多远。

intro.en: Pleasant and please come from one Latin verb, but they entered English as different parts of speech: please as a verb, pleasant as its participle turned adjective.
intro.cn: pleasant 与 please 同出一个拉丁动词，但进入英语时词性不同：please 是动词，pleasant 是由它的分词转成的形容词。

items.en: The verb placere meant to please, to be agreeable, and it was used of things that satisfy a person.
items.cn: 动词 placere 意为使人高兴、令人满意，用来指让人称心的事物。

items.en: Its present participle placens, stem placent-, meant pleasing, the one giving pleasure.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）意为「令人愉悦的」，即正在带来愉悦的那一方。

items.en: Old French turned the participle into plaisant, an adjective meaning pleasing or charming.
items.cn: 古法语把这个分词变成形容词 plaisant，意为令人愉悦的、讨人喜欢的。

items.en: English borrowed plaisant as pleasant, keeping the adjective role, while the verb came in separately as please.
items.cn: 英语借入 plaisant 写作 pleasant，保留形容词身份；动词则另以 please 的形式进入。

items.en: Modern English uses pleasant for places, manners and news, and please for the act of giving pleasure or making a request.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pleasant 形容地方、举止与消息，用 please 表示使人高兴的动作或礼貌请求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the please family and one word with a different origin; the near-meaning group gathers words for what delights or suits us.
note.cn: 形近组收 please 词族，以及一个来源不同的词；近义组收表示使人愉悦或合宜的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give pleasure or to ask politely; pleasant is its old participle.
entries.definitionCN: 表示使人高兴或礼貌请求的动词；pleasant 是它古老的分词形式。

entries.definition: A feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.
entries.definitionCN: 愉快、满足的感觉。

entries.definition: Giving pleasure, often of an experience.
entries.definitionCN: 带来愉悦的，常形容体验。

entries.definition: An urgent request or a statement in court; looks close but comes from Old French plait, a lawsuit.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急请求或法庭陈述；拼写相近，但出自古法语 plait（诉讼），词源不同。

entries.definition: Pleasant and easy to accept or be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快、容易相处或接受的。

entries.definition: Causing great pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 带来很大快乐的。

entries.definition: Giving enjoyment, said of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 令人享受的，多形容活动。

entries.definition: Pleasant or satisfactory in a general, everyday way.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中泛指令人愉快或满意的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of pleasing produced both a verb and an adjective in English; keeping their parts of speech apart is the whole trick.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「使人高兴」的拉丁动词在英语里同时产出了动词和形容词；分清两者的词性就是全部关键。

normal.en: Pleasant is the old participle of please: pleasing, therefore pleasant.
normal.cn: pleasant 是 please 古老的分词形式：正在使人愉悦的，因此是「令人愉快的」。

normal.en: Please is what you do; pleasant is what something is. The verb acts, the adjective describes.
normal.cn: please 是你做的动作；pleasant 是某物的性质。动词做事，形容词描述。

normal.en: Pleasure is the noun of the same family, formed with -ure, naming the feeling itself.
normal.cn: pleasure 是同族的动词名词，用 -ure 构成，指那种感觉本身。

normal.en: Pleasantly adds -ly to the adjective, turning it into the way something is done or felt.
normal.cn: pleasantly 在形容词后加 -ly，把它变成做某事或感受某事的方式。

normal.en: Plea looks similar but belongs to law and requests, not to pleasing.
normal.cn: plea 看着相近，却属于法律与请求的语义，与「愉悦」无关。

abstract.en: The same root gives a verb, an adjective and a noun, which shows how English lets one act spread across three roles.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出动词、形容词和名词，说明英语让一个动作分散到三种角色上。

abstract.en: A word that starts as an action becomes a quality: what pleases for long enough is simply pleasant.
abstract.cn: 一个从动作开始的词变成了性质：使人愉悦得够久，就干脆成了「令人愉快的」。

abstract.en: We call both air and manners pleasant, as if comfort in the body and comfort in company were the same feeling.
abstract.cn: 我们既说空气 pleasant，也说举止 pleasant，仿佛身体的舒适与相处时的舒适是同一种感受。

examples.en: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The staff were pleasant and quick to help.
examples.cn: 员工们态度和善，帮忙很及时。

examples.en: It was a pleasant surprise to see her at the door.
examples.cn: 在门口见到她，是个令人惊喜的意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普莱增特」——一进门就请（please）你坐下，气氛一下子变得舒服。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使人高兴）→ 现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）→ 古法语 plaisant → 英语 pleasant；同族的动词是 please。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of pleasing; the senses spread from the effect on the senses to the warmth of a person and to what suits the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使人愉悦」这个动作；义项从对感官的作用，扩展到人的和善，再到合乎心意之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opens and warmth, light and a faint scent arrive together, so the shoulders loosen without being told.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，暖意、光线与淡淡香气一同涌来，肩膀不必吩咐就松了下来。

branches.en: a wide window and warm light in a small room
branches.cn: 小房间里一扇宽窗与温暖的光

branches.en: a host smiling and pointing to a chair
branches.cn: 主人微笑并示意一把椅子

branches.en: work finished before the sky goes dark
branches.cn: 天还没黑就干完了活

branches.en: comfort that comes from people and from timing
branches.cn: 来自人、也来自时机的舒适

branches.en: the same word for air, music and taste
branches.cn: 同一个词用于空气、音乐与味道

senses.title: A courteous word in a request
senses.definition: used when asking for something or inviting someone to act, so that the request sounds polite
senses.definitionCN: 在提出请求或邀请别人做某事时使用，使语气显得客气
senses.example: Please close the window before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 走之前请把窗户关好。
senses.why: The verb first meant to be agreeable to someone, and the request use keeps that attitude: the speaker puts the other person's comfort first and asks softly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的动词本义是「令某人觉得合意」，请求用法延续的正是这种姿态：说话人先把对方的舒适放在前面，于是请求变得轻而客气。

senses.title: To give someone satisfaction
senses.definition: to make someone feel happy, content or satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 让某人感到高兴、满意或称心
senses.example: The simple answer seemed to please the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个简洁的答复似乎让整个委员会都很满意。
senses.why: Latin placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to a person, so the one who is pleased is always the judge of whether the action worked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令人觉得合意、可接受」，所以被取悦的那个人始终是判断这件事成不成的人。

senses.title: To do as one wishes
senses.titleCN: 随自己的意愿；自行其便
senses.definition: to act according to your own wish rather than someone else's, as in the phrase please yourself
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的想法行事而不迁就别人，常见于 please yourself 这一说法
senses.example: You can please yourself about the seating arrangement.
senses.exampleCN: 座位怎么安排，你随自己的意思就好。
senses.why: If pleasing means making a person content, then pleasing oneself turns that contentment inward: the same verb now names a choice made for the speaker alone.
senses.whyCN: 既然 please 是「让人称心」，那么 please oneself 就是把这份称心转向自己：同一个动词在此指只为说话人自己作的选择。

intro.en: Please goes back to a Latin verb meaning to be agreeable, travelled through French, and in English shrank into the small polite word used in requests.
intro.cn: please 源自一个表示「令人觉得合意」的拉丁动词，经法语传入英语，最后又缩略成请求句里那个轻巧的客套词。

items.en: Placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to someone, and it could describe a person as well as a thing.
items.cn: placere 意为令某人觉得愉快、可以接受，既可以形容事物，也可以形容人。

items.en: The related noun placitum named what seemed good and therefore a decision; it fed plea and plead rather than the verb please itself.
items.cn: 相关的名词 placitum 指「看起来好的事」，引申为决定；它后来生出 plea 与 plead，而不是动词 please 本身。

items.en: Old French used plaisir both as a verb meaning to please and as a noun for the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: 古法语中 plaisir 既是动词「使高兴」，也是名词「随之而来的快乐」。

items.en: Middle English plesen kept the verb and began to use it inside fixed courteous formulas.
items.cn: 中古英语的 plesen 保留了动词用法，并开始在固定的客套句式里使用它。

items.en: Modern English keeps please as a verb, splits off pleased and pleasant as adjectives, and uses the bare form as a courtesy marker.
items.cn: 现代英语让 please 继续作动词，分出 pleased 与 pleasant 两个形容词，又用光杆形式充当礼貌标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin verb for being agreeable; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for satisfying someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「令人合意」这一动词上的同族词；近义组收表示「使满意」的动词。

entries.definition: Feeling happy or satisfied about something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事感到高兴或满意的。

entries.definition: Enjoyable, agreeable or nice to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的；好相处的。

entries.definition: To annoy or upset someone.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不快；惹恼。

entries.definition: An urgent request, or the answer of an accused person in court.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；被告在法庭上的答辩。

entries.definition: To give someone enough of what they want or need.
entries.definitionCN: 满足某人的需要或愿望。

entries.definition: To give someone great pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人极为高兴。

entries.definition: To please someone greatly, often by being attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并取悦某人。

entries.definition: To please someone by satisfying a wish or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 满足愿望而使某人高兴。

normalIntro.en: The family is built on one Latin verb for being agreeable, and its forms keep splitting into the feeling and the cause of the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词建立在同一个表示「令人合意」的拉丁动词上，各个形式不断分成「感受」和「引起感受之物」两侧。

normal.en: Latin placere means to be agreeable to someone, so what pleases is what the other person accepts as good.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令某人觉得合意」，所以能 please 人的东西，就是被对方认可为好而接受的东西。

normal.en: Please yourself puts the same agreement inside the speaker: the wish you agree with is your own.
normal.cn: please yourself 把这种「合意」转向说话人自己：你认同的愿望就是你自己的愿望。

normal.en: Pleased with -ed describes how a person feels; pleasing with -ing describes what produces that feeling.
normal.cn: 加了 -ed 的 pleased 说人心里怎么感觉；加了 -ing 的 pleasing 说是什么东西造成了这种感觉。

normal.en: Pleasant came through French, so it lost the s of please but kept the sense of being agreeable.
normal.cn: pleasant 经由法语而来，因此丢了 please 里的 s，却保留了「合意、讨人喜欢」的意思。

normal.en: The bare please in a request is the old verb worn down to a single polite signal.
normal.cn: 请求句里那个单独的 please，是老动词被磨成了一个纯粹的礼貌信号。

abstract.en: A word that means both make happy and if you would shows that politeness is a small gift of comfort.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能表示「使高兴」又能表示「请」，说明礼貌本身就是送给对方的一点舒适。

abstract.en: Every please hands the decision to the listener for a second, and that second is what makes the request gentle.
abstract.cn: 每一次说 please，都是把决定权交给听者一小会儿，而这一小会儿正是请求变得柔和的原因。

abstract.en: A pleased face, a pleasant evening and a polite request all sit under one root, because all three are about things being acceptable.
abstract.cn: 满意的脸色、宜人的夜晚、客气的请求同出一根，因为三者说的都是「合意」。

examples.en: Please leave your shoes at the door.
examples.cn: 请把鞋留在门口。

examples.en: The children were pleased with the new playground.
examples.cn: 孩子们对新游乐场很满意。

examples.en: She learned to please herself instead of chasing approval.
examples.cn: 她学会按自己的心意生活，而不是一味追求别人的认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑利兹」——把好处扑过去让对方得利，就是「使高兴」；开口求人先递一个「请」。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使愉快、被接受）经古法语 plaisir 进入英语；同族词多与「合意、愉快」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is being agreeable to someone; from it grow the courteous request, the act of giving satisfaction, and the choice to follow one's own wish.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「令某人觉得合意」；由此长出礼貌请求、使人满意这两种用法，以及按自己心意行事的选择。

branches.cn: 孩子对着新玩具咧嘴笑

branches.cn: 主人再添一勺，客人笑着接受

branches.en: a quiet evening that suits everyone
branches.cn: 一个人人满意的安静夜晚

intro.en: One Latin verb for being pleasing holds the family together, and two English suffixes split it into the feeling and the cause of the feeling.
intro.cn: 一个表示「令人愉快」的拉丁动词撑起这一族词，两个英语后缀再把它分成「感受」与「成因」两侧。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
